layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract—Stainless steels of the 18–8 variety at 25°C in 0·1N NaCl or 0·1N NaBr show increasingly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: noble critical pitting potentials, but at 0°C decreasingly noble critical potentials with added per cent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Re. A likely cause is temperature-sensitive hydration effects within the double layer.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: IN A RECENT paper¹ it was shown that Mo alloyed with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stainless steel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shifted the critical pitting potential in 0·1N NaCl in the noble direction corresponding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to the well-known improved resistance of such alloys to pitting corrosion. The noble

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shift of potential, however, was shown to occur only at room and at somewhat above

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: room temperature

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by way of contrast, the effect of Mo was to lower

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the critical pitting potential or to shift it in the active direction corresponding to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decreased resistance to pitting corrosion. Immersion tests in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: confirmed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that whereas pitting of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stainless steel did not occur within two days at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting was observed under the same conditions at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This is opposite to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effect found for 18-8 stainless steel without Mo, pitting being observed at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: but

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: . It was of interest to learn whether alloyed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which is also reported to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improve pitting resistance of 18–8 stainless steel,² shows a similar temperature effect.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Alloys were prepared by vacuum melting in dense alumina crucibles decarburized

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: electrolytic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: International Nickel Company. Re containing 15ppm Fe but less than 1ppm of any

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: other detectable impurity was supplied by courtesy of Ledgemont Laboratory,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Kennecott Copper Corporation. The melt was cast in a purified argon atmosphere

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by drawing into 7mm dia. Vycor tubes and quenching in water. The alloys were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: homogenized at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for 17h, swaged to 0·4cm dia. rods, annealed at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: water quenched. They were mostly austenitic as quenched, being only slightly magnetic.

layout_dets.text: Mo- compared to the Re-stainless steels. As is discussed in the earlier reference¹ these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
